cells: Salary charged on Consolidated Fund of India

blocks.content: The CAG shall only be removed from office in like manner and on the like grounds as a Judge of the Supreme Court.

rows: Does not control the issue of money from the exchequer
Has full control; money cannot be issued without consent

items: CAG's salary and office expenses are charged upon the Consolidated Fund of India and are not subject to the vote of Parliament.
After retirement or removal, CAG is strictly prohibited from holding any further office under the Central or State Governments.
CAG can be removed only on the basis of a resolution passed by both Houses of Parliament with a special majority on grounds of proved misbehaviour or incapacity.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The CAG is provided with security of tenure and can be removed by the President only in the manner and on the grounds similar to a Supreme Court judge.
The CAG is not eligible for further office either under the Government of India or any state government after ceasing to hold office.
Salary and other service conditions of the CAG are determined by Parliament and cannot be varied to their disadvantage after appointment.
Administrative expenses of the office of CAG, including all salaries, allowances, and pensions, are charged upon the Consolidated Fund of India and are non-votable.
